summary: Elizabeth “Liz” Uihlein co-founded Uline with her husband, Richard, and runs the private shipping-supplies company as chief executive. She is independently one of the Republican Party's largest donors and uses Uline's widely distributed catalog and website to publish her own views on government, labor, trade, public health and social policy.

chapters.title: Family and partnership
chapters.dek: A marriage becomes a business and political partnership
chapters.body:
Elizabeth Uihlein was born in 1945 and grew up in the Chicago area. She married Richard Uihlein before his 1967 Stanford graduation, entering a family whose business history and conservative politics would become part of their shared public identity [[nyt-uihleins-2018, propublica-box-empire-2022]].

The couple's public record is often aggregated, but they are separate actors. Each reports contributions under an individual name, and in 2026 they backed opposing candidates in the same Wisconsin congressional primary [[fec-elizabeth, ap-wisconsin-primary-2026]].

chapters.title: The operator behind Uline
chapters.dek: Service discipline and a private-company fortune
chapters.body:
Liz and Dick Uihlein founded Uline in their basement in 1980, beginning with a carton-sizing product. The company expanded across North America into packaging, industrial, safety and material-handling supplies [[uline-history]].

Uline identifies Elizabeth as chief executive. Reporting describes her as the hands-on operator responsible for next-day shipping, tightly specified workplace practices and a customer-service culture that helped turn the company into a multibillion-dollar private enterprise [[uline-history, propublica-box-empire-2022]].

chapters.title: A catalog as a political platform
chapters.dek: The chief executive writes directly to customers
chapters.body:
Elizabeth's role differs from that of a donor who speaks only through checks. Her “From the President” letters appear in Uline catalogs and online, mixing corporate stories with arguments about taxes, trade, marijuana, news media, public policy and social change [[uline-president, wapo-richard-2018]].

The archive supplies unusually direct evidence of her views, but dates and versions are not always easy to reconstruct. Statements in this profile therefore cite an identified letter or contemporary reporting rather than treating every reposted image as authentic [[uline-president, uline-nafta]].

chapters.title: An independent donor record
chapters.dek: Household rankings can hide who signed each check
chapters.body:
Elizabeth became a major federal donor in her own name, generally favoring national party committees and congressional outside groups. That pattern has sometimes differed from Richard's heavier use of candidate-specific and ideological super PACs [[fec-elizabeth, opensecrets-uihleins-2022]].

OpenSecrets placed the couple's combined 2024-cycle giving near $143.5 million. The household number explains their joint scale; the FEC ledger on this profile is deliberately narrower and attributes only records matched to Elizabeth [[opensecrets-2024, fec-elizabeth]].

chapters.title: Shared institutions
chapters.dek: The Uihlein political network extends beyond candidate committees
chapters.body:
Elizabeth's giving overlaps with Richard's through Trump-aligned groups, congressional committees and the Restoration network. Restoration-funded projects have included voter-file work, advertising and partisan publications presented in local-news formats [[propublica-voteref-2022, propublica-catholic-tribune-2024]].

Evidence of a donation establishes financial support, not operational control. Richard is the documented principal funder of Restoration PAC, so the network is included here only where records or reporting connect Elizabeth directly or describe joint household activity [[propublica-box-empire-2022]].

chapters.title: Business policy and public policy
chapters.dek: Trade, labor and regulation cross the company boundary
chapters.body:
Uline's commercial interests make some of Elizabeth's political writing directly relevant to the business. She has written about NAFTA and China, while the company has lobbied on truck-driver hours and other distribution rules [[uline-nafta, atlantic-duffy-2026]].

Two reported controversies require careful attribution. ProPublica documented Uline's successful later visa petition after a denial; the Guardian later reported allegations about Mexican employees working in U.S. facilities, which Uline disputed. Neither episode by itself proves hypocrisy or unlawful conduct by Elizabeth [[propublica-immigration-2019, guardian-uihlein-workers-2025]].

chapters.title: Alignment without uniformity
chapters.dek: A Republican donor who sometimes parts company with allies
chapters.body:
Elizabeth has funded Trump-aligned groups, but her own writing and reported internal messages show criticism as well as support. In 2025 she reportedly circulated a cartoon mocking Trump's account of trade leverage with China [[propublica-immigration-2019, guardian-cartoon-2025]].

The 2026 Wisconsin primary made the distinction between the spouses concrete: she gave $1 million to a group supporting Jessie Rodriguez Ebben while Richard backed a rival. A shared company, marriage and broad partisan alignment do not erase separate political judgment [[ap-wisconsin-primary-2026]].

chapters.title: Present influence
chapters.dek: Corporate reach, personal speech and political money
chapters.body:
As of October 2026, Elizabeth remains Uline's chief executive, a catalog columnist and an active donor. Those roles reinforce one another: company ownership produces resources, the catalog supplies an audience and contributions finance political organizations [[uline-history, uline-president, fec-elizabeth]].

The public record is still incomplete. Uline is private, Forbes does not separate the spouses' ownership into defensible individual fortunes and state reporting sits outside the federal ledger. The profile therefore reports the source of wealth and each disclosed contribution rather than assigning Elizabeth half of a household estimate [[forbes-richard-2026, fec-elizabeth]].
